terra.problem: Saying Daniel is about to get the entire operation treats the king’s plan as a settled outcome. The text says only that the king planned to set him over the kingdom.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the facts, without Papa Dorin’s personality in a moment that could hold some humor.
The text does not say how Daniel worked when nobody was checking.
The explanation is generic and repetitive, with little of Papa Dorin’s voice in a moment that could be livelier.
Saying no night shift was added assumes Daniel did not pray at night. The text does not specify the times of his prayers.
The windows opened toward Jerusalem. Calling it a view suggests Jerusalem could be seen from them, which the text does not say.
The text says the windows opened toward Jerusalem, not that Daniel faced that direction when he prayed.
This is a flat restatement of the detail, without Papa Dorin’s personality.
The text says the king labored until sundown, not that he spent the day doing so.
The text does not say nobody was laughing. It reports the king’s distress, not everyone’s reaction.
The text says Darius labored until sundown, not that he worked for a whole day.
A full day of effort adds a duration the text does not give. It says he labored until sundown.
The seal’s stated purpose was to prevent anything concerning Daniel from being changed. The text does not guarantee that nobody could sneak in and move the stone.
Daniel says God sent His angel and shut the lions’ mouths. The text does not say that the angel went into the den.

Daniel says he had done no wrong against the king, not that he had done nothing to him. The accusers also reported true details, including that Daniel prayed three times a day, so it overstates the text to say they had nothing true to say.
The text says the king fasted that night, but it does not say whether Daniel fasted.
Saying Darius learned firsthand that God’s kingdom has no end goes beyond the text. He witnessed Daniel’s rescue and declared that God’s kingdom and dominion endure.
